classes.name: Val till riksdagen
classes.finest_note: Valmyndigheten publishes votes by election district (valdistrikt) from 2002; SCB's database reports by municipality and constituency from 1973, and the SOS volume of each election back to 1970 reports by election district.
classes.note: The unicameral Riksdag since 1971: 349 members (350 in 1970 and 1973) in 29 constituencies (28 until 1991) with fixed constituency seats and 39 (40) national adjustment seats, a 4 percent national threshold or 12 percent in a constituency, and optional preference votes. Three-year terms until 1994, four years since.

classes.disposition_reason: The First Chamber (1867–1970) was chosen by the county councils and the councils of towns outside the counties, not by voters; its members appear with the councils that elected them.

classes.name: Ståndsriksdagen
classes.disposition_reason: The four estates chose their members by estate-specific procedures (nobles by birth, clergy and burghers through their own bodies, peasants through electors); no official returns were published before the Estates gave way to the bicameral Riksdag in 1866.

classes.name: Val till regionfullmäktige (landstingsfullmäktige)
classes.finest_note: Valmyndigheten publishes election-district results from 2002; SCB's database by municipality and region from 1973.
classes.note: Councils of the county councils (landsting), renamed regions from 2019; elected on the general election day since 1970 by list PR, with a 3 percent threshold, and in one or more constituencies per region. One contest per region. Göteborg and Malmö stood outside the county councils until 1998; Gotland's municipality has held the regional duties throughout.

classes.name_en: Town and rural municipal council elections before 1971
classes.finest_note: SOS Kommunala valen 1919–1966 reports by municipality; earlier town-council elections have no national returns.
classes.note: Town councils (stadsfullmäktige) from 1863 and rural and market-town councils (kommunalfullmäktige), compulsory in larger municipalities from 1919 and everywhere from 1952; graded votes until 1919, list PR after. classes.name: Val till kyrkomötet
classes.name_en: Church of Sweden General Synod elections
classes.finest_note: Svenska kyrkan publishes results by diocese constituency, with local breakdowns from 2013.
classes.note: Members of the Church of Sweden elect the 251-member General Synod directly since 2001, by list PR in diocese constituencies, on the same days as the diocese and parish council elections (kyrkoval). Before the church's separation from the state in 2000 the synod was chosen indirectly.

cadence.administered_by: Svenska kyrkan (Kyrkokansliet and the diocese election boards)

access.evidence: Downloadable results for 2001–2021 and local presentations for the synod, diocese, and parish council elections of 2013–2025.
Final 2025 results by body and constituency.

classes.name: Val till stiftsfullmäktige och kyrkofullmäktige
classes.name_en: Church of Sweden diocese and parish council elections
classes.note: The 13 diocese councils (stiftsfullmäktige) and the parish or pastorate councils (kyrkofullmäktige) are elected with the General Synod by church members.

access.evidence: Diocese-council results 2013–2025 and parish-council results 2025 as local presentations; 2001–2021 summaries as xlsx.

classes.name: Kyrkliga val före 2000
classes.name_en: Church elections under the state church, before 2000
classes.note: Parish meetings and, from 1930, elected parish councils (kyrkofullmäktige) under public law, with direct diocese elections from 1983.
classes.disposition_reason: No national returns: the parish elections of the state church were reported only in parish and diocese minutes, and neither SCB nor Svenska kyrkan publishes results before 2001.

classes.name: Statschef (konung)
classes.disposition_reason: The monarch is hereditary under the Act of Succession (successionsordningen); no executive office is elected.

classes.name: Statsminister
classes.disposition_reason: The Speaker proposes a prime minister and the Riksdag tolerates the nominee unless a majority votes against (RF 6 kap. 4 §); the government is not elected by voters.

classes.name: Kommunstyrelsens och regionstyrelsens ordförande
classes.disposition_reason: Executive boards and their chairs (kommunalråd, regionråd) are elected by the councils (kommunallagen 6 kap.), not by voters.

classes.name: Kommunalförbund och gemensamma nämnder
classes.disposition_reason: Joint authorities (kommunalförbund) and joint committees are appointed by the member councils (kommunallagen 9 kap.); no special-purpose body is elected directly.

classes.name: Nämndemän och domare
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are appointed by the government; lay judges (nämndemän) are chosen by the municipal and regional councils (rättegångsbalken 4 kap. 7 §), not by voters.

classes.name: Provval inom partier
classes.disposition_reason: Parties nominate their own candidates, some through internal member ballots (provval); the state runs no nominating contest and the ballots are not public returns.

classes.name: Riksdagens utnämning av Europaparlamentariker 1995
classes.name_en: Members of the European Parliament appointed by the Riksdag, January–October 1995
classes.disposition_reason: From accession on 1 January 1995 until the first direct election, Sweden's 22 members were appointed by the Riksdag from among its members.
